joshua-18:12:1.summary: Joshua 7:2 mentions Ai near “Bethel,” but not Bethon, the wilderness named in the source.
joshua-18:12:1.why: Shown wording lacks the Beth-aven link.

joshua-18:12:3.summary: Hosea’s “house of On” may correspond to the source’s “Bethon,” but the names only loosely match.
joshua-18:12:3.why: Possible later prophetic mention of the same place.

joshua-18:12:5.summary: The “house of On” with its calf may be the source’s Bethon, but the identification is not explicit.
joshua-18:12:5.why: Possible later reference to the place as an idol site.

joshua-18:12:6.summary: Hosea’s “house of On” beside Benjamin may be Bethon on Benjamin’s border, but names only loosely match.
joshua-18:12:6.why: Possible later reference to the border place.

joshua-18:13:0.summary: The source equates Luza with Bethel; Genesis names the place “House of God,” formerly “Oulamlous,” which contains Luz.
joshua-18:13:0.why: Explains the origin of Bethel’s name.

joshua-18:13:4.summary: “Descent of Horonin” likely refers to Beth-horon named in the source, but the name is only partly shared.
joshua-18:13:4.why: Links the border town to Joshua’s battle.

joshua-18:14:4.summary: The source calls Kiriath-jearim “a city of the sons of Judah”; Chronicles brings the ark from “the city of Jarim,” “which belonged to Judah.”
joshua-18:14:4.why: Shows the border town’s later role housing the ark.

joshua-18:16:0.summary: The source’s valley of Onnam/Gaienna is the “valley of the son of Ennom” where Josiah defiled Tapheth.
joshua-18:16:0.why: Shows the border valley’s later idolatrous history.

joshua-18:16:7.summary: The source’s “Gaienna” corresponds to “Gaibenenom,” where Ahaz sacrificed his children.
joshua-18:16:7.why: Shows the border valley’s later idolatrous history.

joshua-18:16:10.summary: The valley on Benjamin’s border is the “Son of Hinnom” place Jeremiah says will be renamed for slaughter.

joshua-18:16:14.summary: The source’s “Emekraphain” corresponds to the “Valley of the Giants” (Rephaim) where the foreigners attacked David.
joshua-18:16:14.why: Locates a later battle site on the border.

joshua-18:16:15.summary: The source’s valley of Onnam is the “Valley of the Son of Hinnom” where Baal altars were built.
joshua-18:16:15.why: Shows the valley’s later idolatrous use.

joshua-18:16:16.summary: The source’s “Gaienna” corresponds to “Gai-banai-ennom,” where Manasseh passed his children through fire.
joshua-18:16:16.why: Shows the valley’s later idolatrous use.

joshua-18:16:17.summary: The border valley is the “ravine of the son of Hinnom” of Topheth, renamed “Ravine of the Slain.”
joshua-18:16:17.why: Shows the valley’s later infamy and judgment.

joshua-18:21:4.summary: The source’s “Betheglio” corresponds to “Beth-hoglah” on Benjamin’s border in the preceding description.
joshua-18:21:4.why: Ties the city list to the boundary description.

joshua-18:21:6.summary: The source’s “Betheglio” corresponds to “Beth-hoglah” on Judah’s boundary.
joshua-18:21:6.why: Shows the town sits on the Judah–Benjamin border.

joshua-18:22:0.summary: “The Zemarite” is unrelated to the source’s “Sara”; the Greek-based names do not carry a link.

joshua-18:22:1.summary: “Mount Somoron” does not match the source’s “Sara” or other names shown.

joshua-18:22:2.summary: The source’s “Bethabara” may be a form of “Beth-arabah” on Benjamin’s border, but spellings differ.
